subject: ela
intro: This test covers the whole Key Ideas and Details cluster for literature across all three standards: answering questions with text evidence (3.RL.A.1), central message (3.RL.A.2), and describing characters and their effect on events (3.RL.A.3). Each question is multiple choice and labeled with the standard it checks.

items.prompt:
Read the story.

On Tuesday, Kofi brought carrots and lettuce to school in a bag to feed the class rabbit.

WHAT did Kofi bring to feed the rabbit?
A) Carrots and lettuce
B) Bread and cheese
C) Seeds and water
D) Apples and nuts

steps: The question asks WHAT he brought.
The story says "carrots and lettuce."
The answer is A.

items.prompt:
Read the story.

Because the road was flooded, the school bus took the long way and arrived ten minutes late.

WHY was the bus late?
A) It ran out of gas
B) The road was flooded
C) The driver was sick
D) It was snowing

steps: The question asks WHY.
The story says "the road was flooded."
So the answer is B.

items.prompt:
Read the story.

The science project needed sunlight, so Lena moved the plant from the dark corner to the bright windowsill. A week later it had three new leaves.

WHY did the plant grow new leaves?
A) Lena watered it less
B) Lena moved it into the sunlight
C) The corner got darker
D) It was winter
items.answer: B) Lena moved it into the sunlight

steps: The plant "needed sunlight."
Lena moved it to "the bright windowsill."
The sunlight made it grow, so B.
solution.answer: B) Lena moved it into the sunlight

items.prompt:
Read the fable.

A hare bragged and napped during a race, while a steady tortoise plodded on and won.

What is the lesson?
A) Bragging helps
B) Slow and steady wins the race
C) Naps are important
D) Hares are lazy
items.answer: B) Slow and steady wins the race

steps: The tortoise won by staying "steady."
The bragging hare lost.
The lesson is B.
solution.answer: B) Slow and steady wins the race

items.prompt:
Read the story.

Eli saved half his allowance every week instead of spending it all. By summer he had enough to buy the bike his family could not afford.

What central message does this story teach?
A) Bikes are fun
B) Saving a little at a time adds up
C) Summer is long
D) Allowances are small
items.answer: B) Saving a little at a time adds up

steps: Eli "saved half his allowance every week."
By summer he had "enough to buy the bike."
Small savings added up, so B.
solution.answer: B) Saving a little at a time adds up

items.prompt:
Read the story.

Everyone laughed when quiet Sam spent months building a strange wooden box. When the flood came, that box floated the neighborhood's important papers to safety.

Which sentence best states the story's message?
A) Floods are dangerous
B) Boxes float on water
C) Do not laugh at ideas you do not yet understand
D) Sam works slowly
items.answer: C) Do not laugh at ideas you do not yet understand

steps: People "laughed" at Sam's strange box.
The box later "floated the... papers to safety."
The odd idea turned out valuable, so C.
solution.answer: C) Do not laugh at ideas you do not yet understand

items.prompt:
Read the story.

When the new kid dropped his books, thoughtful Amina stopped and helped him pick every one up.

Which word best describes Amina?
A) Thoughtful
B) Rude
C) Lazy
D) Angry

steps: Amina "stopped and helped him pick every one up."
Helping shows she is thoughtful.
The answer is A.

items.prompt:
Read the story.

Restless Theo could not sit still and kept tapping his pencil until it flew across the room and interrupted the whole class.

How does Theo's restlessness affect the events?
A) It helps him finish his work
B) It causes his pencil to fly and interrupt class
C) It makes him fall asleep
D) It has no effect
items.answer: B) It causes his pencil to fly and interrupt class

steps: Theo is "restless" and "kept tapping his pencil."
The pencil "flew across the room" and interrupted class.
His restlessness caused it, so B.
solution.answer: B) It causes his pencil to fly and interrupt class

items.prompt:
Read the story.

At first Bea was too shy to sing, but after her friendcheered her on, she felt braver and sang the solo.

How do Bea's feelings change?
A) From brave to shy
B) From shy to braver
C) From angry to sad
D) They stay the same

steps: At first Bea is "too shy to sing."
After being cheered, she "felt braver" and sang.
So her feelings change from shy to braver, B.

items.prompt:
Read the story.

Careful Nadia noticed the loose railing on the bridge and warned everyone to hold the far side. Minutes later the loose rail gave way, but no one was leaning on it.

How does Nadia's careful nature shape what happens?
A) It causes the railing to break
B) Her warning keeps everyone safe when the rail gives way
C) It slows the group down
D) It has no effect on the events
items.answer: B) Her warning keeps everyone safe when the rail gives way

steps: Nadia "noticed the loose railing" and "warned everyone."
When it "gave way," "no one was leaning on it."
Her care kept them safe, so B.
solution.answer: B) Her warning keeps everyone safe when the rail gives way

items.prompt:
Read the story.

The twins wanted the last kite. Instead of fighting, generous Lia offered to fly it together, taking turns holding the string. By the end, the twins were laughing and had made a new friend in Lia.

Which answer best explains how Lia's trait shapes the ending?
A) Her greed starts a fight
B) Her generosity turns a conflict into a new friendship
C) Her anger ends the game
D) Her shyness keeps her away
items.answer: B) Her generosity turns a conflict into a new friendship

steps: Lia is "generous" and "offered to fly it together."
The twins ended up "laughing" and made "a new friend."
Her generosity created friendship, so B.
solution.answer: B) Her generosity turns a conflict into a new friendship

items.prompt:
Read the story.

Grandma always told Nia, "Measure twice, cut once." Nia rushed her craft and cut the paper too short, ruining it, then remembered the saying and measured carefully the second time.

What is the central message, and how do Nia's actions show it?
A) Crafts are hard; her paper tore
B) Rushing can cause mistakes, so it is better to be careful; Nia ruins her first try but succeeds when careful
C) Grandmas give advice; Nia ignores it forever
D) Paper is expensive; Nia buys more
items.answer: B) Rushing can cause mistakes, so it is better to be careful; Nia ruins her first try but succeeds when careful

steps: Nia "rushed" and "cut the paper too short, ruining it."
When she "measured carefully the second time," it worked.
The message is to be careful, not rush, so B.
solution.answer: B) Rushing can cause mistakes, so it is better to be careful; Nia ruins her first try but succeeds when careful
